Key Research Thinking Patterns: Geospatial Data Fusion for Safety Correlation: Integrating disparate roadway inventory databases with national fatality reporting systems (FARS) using coordinate system translation and blackspot analysis to identify physical infrastructure factors linked to fatal crashes.

Hardware-Accelerated Context Switching: Designing a Shared Context Unit (SCU) with crossbar switch interconnects to enable low-overhead, fine-grained thread migration between cores, achieving context switch latencies of two cycles compared to software-based OS mechanisms.

Runahead Pre-Execution for In-Order Pipelines: Leveraging cycle-accurate simulation of SPEC CPU2006 benchmarks to demonstrate that in-order processors significantly benefit from reusing results from pre-executed instructions to eliminate redundant independent instruction chain execution.

Adaptive Frame Management for Low-Bandwidth ITS: Implementing rate control strategies that adaptively drop frames prior to H.264/AVC encoding and replicate retained frames to maintain spatial quality and reduce decoder errors in heterogeneous vehicular networks.
Summary Description: Ronald Barnes specializes in the intersection of high-performance computer architecture and intelligent transportation systems. His research bridges hardware-level optimizations, such as low-latency context switching via Shared Context Units and runahead pre-execution for in-order pipelines, with macro-level safety applications. He develops methodologies for correlating roadway inventory data with fatality statistics to inform highway safety planning. Additionally, he designs robust video compression and distribution strategies for ITS networks, ensuring high-quality traffic surveillance under bandwidth constraints. His work on connected vehicle prototypes using DSRC and CAN bus interfacing further demonstrates a commitment to real-time hazard detection and driver safety enhancement in adverse weather conditions.
